text:
Maya Chen: Hey benefits team — short one: I had to get a PCR/NAAT test for an airline-required pre-travel check last week (company trip). My receipt shows lab billed $165 and my insurer marked it 'Not covered — screening/preventive'. Can I get reimbursed or is there an appeal route?

Raj Patel: Hi Maya — sorry that happened. Two quick things: 1) many plans treat asymptomatic travel/entry tests as non-covered. 2) we can still submit a claim and request an exception if you can provide documentation that this was for a business trip. Please upload the itemized lab invoice + payment receipt + the airline/travel requirement showing the date.

Maya Chen: Thanks — I have the PDF from the airline and the receipt attached in the benefits portal. Is there a special code I should ask the lab to include?

Raj Patel: If the lab charged CPT 87635 (SARS-CoV-2 NAAT) that’s fine. The important bits are: itemized invoice showing CPT code or test name, proof of payment, and a short note tying the test to business travel. In the portal when you submit choose "Out-of-Network claim" (even though lab is in-network we just need the docs).

Jenna Alvarez: Maya, if you want, People Ops can provide a short "confirmation of business travel" letter you can upload with the claim. Ping me and I’ll generate it.

Maya Chen: Would that actually change coverage or just speed up processing?

Raj Patel: It won't change the plan's published coverage automatically, but claims reviewers consider business-related documentation when evaluating exceptions. It increases the chance of reimbursement on appeal.

Maya Chen: What’s the timeline if I submit now? I need to settle the card charge.

Raj Patel: Standard adjudication is ~7–10 business days after full docs are received. We can request an expedited review for business-critical travel reimbursements — that usually gets a decision in 48–72 hours but is not guaranteed. If you want escalation, react with :arrow_up: and I’ll flag it.

Maya Chen: Flagging now. :arrow_up: Also adding Jenna for the travel confirmation letter.

benefits-bot: Claim submitted: case #B-20270518-4932. Status: awaiting documents. Link: https://benefits.redwood.com/claims/B-20270518-4932

Finance Ops: FYI if it gets approved and needs reimbursement to corporate card vs personal card, we’ll need the payment method note. If charged to corporate card we can do chargeback; if personal, reimbursement to bank account — include W-9 if amount >$600.

Maya Chen: Got it. Uploading now (invoice + airline PDF + payment receipt). Thanks for the quick help everyone.

Raj Patel: Received. I’ll request expedited review and attach a short cover note. Expect an update here once adjudicated.

Maya Chen: Appreciate it :pray:

Jenna Alvarez: On it — I’ll DM you the travel confirmation letter in a minute.

Raj Patel: Closing loop later with outcome so others can reference — if anyone else sees this, please follow the same doc checklist: itemized invoice, proof of payment, travel requirement, and business confirmation if applicable.
